scenes.text: Their legs carry tiny sensors called chemoreceptors, which work like our taste buds.
When a butterfly lands, those sensors pick up the chemicals underneath it.
Mothers use this to choose where to lay their eggs.
A female drums on a leaf with her feet to release the plant's juices.
Her caterpillars feed only on certain plants, so she has to get it right.
If the chemicals match and the plant is safe, she lays her egg.
Adult butterflies can't chew; they drink through a long, straw-like tongue called a proboscis.
When it's not in use, it stays curled up like a garden hose.
A newly emerged butterfly must join two halves of it into one tube before it can drink.
Their antennae pick up smells drifting in the air, like the scent of a mate.
Flower nectar is low in salt, so many butterflies sip from mud puddles.
Most puddle drinkers are males, gathering minerals they later pass to females.
That's also why a butterfly may land on you: it's after the salt in your sweat.
If you could taste with your feet, what would you never walk on?

title: Butterflies taste with their feet 🦋
caption: Butterflies have taste sensors (chemoreceptors) on their feet. Females drum on leaves to taste them before laying eggs, so their caterpillars hatch on the right plant. 🦋
